{{Short description|German mathematician (1899–1942)}}
'''Hildegard Rothe-Ille''', born '''Hildegard Ille''', (1899–1942), was a German [[mathematician]].<ref name="Grünbaum Soifer Johnson Rousseau 2008 p. 332">{{cite book | last=Grünbaum | first=B. | last2=Soifer | first2=A. | author2link= Alexander Soifer |last3=Johnson | first3=P. | last4=Rousseau | first4=C. | title=The Mathematical Coloring Book: Mathematics of Coloring and the Colorful Life of its Creators | publisher=Springer New York | series=Mathematics and Statistics | year=2008 | isbn=978-0-387-74642-5 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Vn3GLf-4YkEC&pg=PA332 | access-date=2022-05-14 | page=332}}</ref><ref name=macbio2>{{MacTutor Biography|title= Hildegard Rothe-Ille|id=Rothe-Ille}}</ref>

==Career==
She was one of [[Issai Schur]]’s doctoral students.<ref name="Bergmann Epple Ungar 2012 p. 53">{{cite book | last=Bergmann | first=B. | last2=Epple | first2=M. |author2-link=Moritz Epple | last3=Ungar | first3=R. | title=Transcending Tradition: Jewish Mathematicians in German Speaking Academic Culture | publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg | year=2012 | isbn=978-3-642-22464-5 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7z8DTwXGO-oC&pg=PA53 | access-date=2022-05-14 | page=53}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Rothe-Ille/poster/lived/|title=Hildegard Ille - Poster|website=Maths History}}</ref> According to [[Alexander Soifer]], “[[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden|Van der Waerden]] walked away from Ramseyan prehistory. Issai Schur, on the other hand, continued to produce Ramseyan mathematics, and moreover directed and inspired his PhD students [[Richard Rado]], Hildegard Ille and [[Alfred Brauer]] to do the same.”<ref>[[Alexander Soifer|A Soifer]], “Ramsey Theory Before Ramsey, Prehistory and Early History: An Essay in 13 Parts”, in [[Alexander Soifer|A Soifer]] (ed.), ''Ramsey Theory: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow'' (Springer Science & Business Media, New York, 2010)</ref>

She received her [[doctorate]] in mathematics in 1924.<ref name=macbio2/><ref>In chapter 34: “Whose Conjecture Did [[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden|Van der Waerden]] Prove? Two Lives between Two Wars: Issai Schur and Pierre Joseph Henry Baudet (in ''The Mathematical Coloring Book: Mathematics of Coloring and the Colorful Life of its Creators'', by Grünbaum, B.; [[Alexander Soifer|Soifer, A.]]; Johnson, P.; Rousseau, C. (2008). Mathematics and Statistics. Springer New York.)</ref> Beginning on April 1, 1925, she was a year-long scholarship holder at the [[Kaiser Wilhelm Society#Kaiser Wilhelm Institutes|Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics]], which was headed by [[Albert Einstein]] at the time.<ref>[[Cornelia Denz]], Annette Vogt. “Hildegard Ille - Stipendiatin am KWI für Physik”, ''Einsteins Kolleginnen - Physikerinnen gestern & heute'' (Kompetenzzentrum Technik, Bielefeld, 2005), pages 13-14, ISBN 978-3-933476-08-1</ref> She was the only woman to receive a scholarship from that institute in that academic year, and she received a higher scholarship than her male counterparts did.<ref name=macbio2/>

She taught at the Chamisso school in Berlin-Schöneberg from 1926 until 1928. After marrying in 1928, due to German law she was not allowed to work for pay; however, she did review papers about mathematics.<ref name=macbio2/> Under the name Hildegard Rothe she reviewed 40 papers which had been published between 1926 and 1928, and under the name Hildegard Rothe-Ille she reviewed 129 papers which had been published between 1930 and 1937.<ref name=macbio2/>

The 1940 [[United States census]] records that she was a part-time teacher of German at [[William Penn University|William Penn College]].<ref name=macbio2/>

==Publications==
* “Zur Irreduzibilität der Kugelfunktionen”. [[Dissertation]], 1924
* “Einige Bemerkungen zu einem von [[George Pólya|G. Pólya]] herrührenden Irreduzibilitätskriterium”. In: Annual report of the [[German Mathematical Society]]. Volume 35, 1926, pages 204–208

==Personal life==
Her parents were Agnes Clara Bertha Thurm and Otto Friedrich Carl Ille. Otto died in 1900.<ref name=macbio2/>

She married [[Erich Rothe]] in 1928. In [[Wrocław|Breslau]] in April 1931 she gave birth to Erhard W. Rothe.<ref name=macbio>{{MacTutor Biography|title=Erich Hans Rothe|id=Rothe_Erich}}</ref>

She and Erich and their son Erhard left [[Nazi Germany]] and arrived in [[Zürich]] in 1937.<ref>W Kaplan, A tribute to Erich H Rothe, Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 12 (1965), 380-381.</ref><ref name=macbio2/> Erich went to the United States after this, and Hildegard and Erhard followed in 1938.<ref name=macbio2/>
